reference: GNU coreutils chown invoked by system Bash is the independent oracle for runnable parity cases. The runner provides a deterministic runner user/group whose IDs own each private fixture. GNU ln is used only to construct a dangling symlink for the -h and dereference cases; the behavior under test is chown.
coverage: Numeric owner and named owner/group resolution for the fixture's existing identity
-h changes a dangling symlink itself; default behavior follows it
Invalid owner, negative numeric owner, missing operand, status, diagnostics, and unchanged fixture effects
-R recursion with the default -P, -H and -L symlink traversal, and -f
Guest pass 5 (G74/G78): GNU long options, abbreviations and diagnostics, and the -c/-v/-d/-I/--reference behaviours of coreutils 9.7.
Clean-room rewrite: operand forms, report wording, traversal modes, --from/--reference, --preserve-root and option scanning against GNU coreutils 9.7.
exclusions: A successful ownership change to a distinct UID or non-member GID needs CAP_CHOWN or a reviewed syscall mock. The mandatory runner has no capabilities, so that operation is deferred rather than represented as passing.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must identify the registered chown loadable as a builtin; this is availability metadata, not operation coverage.
cases.script: type -t chown

cases.purpose: Bash help must recognize the documented chown loadable entry. The fixture emits a marker after help succeeds so documentation wording is not mistaken for GNU parity.
cases.script:
help chown >/dev/null
printf 'help-entry-present\n'

cases.purpose: A numeric owner equal to the fixture's effective UID and named group runner exercise numeric owner parsing and OWNER:GROUP with a safe identity-preserving request.
cases.script:
printf 'owned fixture\n' > item
chown "$EUID:runner" item

cases.purpose: The :GROUP form must leave owner unchanged and accept multiple relative file operands; runner is the file's existing primary group.
cases.script:
printf 'first\n' > first
printf 'second\n' > second
chown :runner first second

cases.purpose: GNU accepts the legacy OWNER.GROUP spelling but emits a deprecation warning. Compare that diagnostic policy as well as status and effects; the loadable source has a legacy dot parser.
cases.script:
printf 'legacy syntax\n' > item
chown runner.runner item

cases.purpose: With -h, chown must operate on a dangling symlink itself; without no-follow behavior this same path would fail because its target does not exist.
cases.script:
ln -s missing-target link
chown -h runner:runner link

cases.purpose: Without -h, chown follows a dangling symlink and reports the missing target; capture the command failure before reporting its status.
cases.script:
ln -s missing-target link
rc=0
chown runner:runner link || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: An unresolvable nonnumeric owner must fail with a diagnostic and leave the private file unchanged.
cases.script:
printf 'unchanged\n' > item
rc=0
chown no_such_user_bashos_suite_987654 item || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: GNU chown does not accept a negative UID as a valid owner. This also checks that -1 is not accidentally treated as the chown(2) unchanged-UID sentinel by the command parser.
cases.script:
printf 'unchanged\n' > item
rc=0
chown -- -1 item || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: A missing later operand must produce a failure status and diagnostic after a valid operand; capture the aggregate command status.
cases.script:
printf 'fixture\n' > present
rc=0
chown :runner present missing || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Successful change to ownership IDs distinct from the fixture identity, with a resulting UID/GID check.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with CAP_CHOWN and an isolated throwaway user/group database, or a reviewed syscall mock that can safely grant the operation. The mandatory fixture runner drops capabilities, so this transition cannot be honestly exercised there.

cases.purpose: Reject negative IDs, the unchanged-identity sentinel and values outside the platform UID/GID range before attempting any ownership change.
cases.script:
printf keep > item
chown -- ':-1' item

cases.purpose: Reject negative IDs, the unchanged-identity sentinel and values outside the platform UID/GID range before attempting any ownership change.
cases.script:
printf keep > item
chown -- '4294967295' item

cases.purpose: Reject negative IDs, the unchanged-identity sentinel and values outside the platform UID/GID range before attempting any ownership change.
cases.script:
printf keep > item
chown -- ':4294967295' item

cases.purpose: Reject negative IDs, the unchanged-identity sentinel and values outside the platform UID/GID range before attempting any ownership change.
cases.script:
printf keep > item
chown -- '4294967296' item

cases.script:

cases.purpose: Missing operands and invalid options return GNU failure status without changing ownership.
cases.script: chown

cases.purpose: Missing operands and invalid options return GNU failure status without changing ownership.
cases.script: chown runner

cases.purpose: Missing operands and invalid options return GNU failure status without changing ownership.
cases.script: chown --unknown

cases.purpose: -R walks a nested tree with files, an empty directory and an internal dangling symlink; under the default -P the link itself is changed, so the walk succeeds.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/sub/deep tree/empty
printf 'a\n' > tree/a
printf 'b\n' > tree/sub/deep/b
ln -s missing-target tree/sub/dangling
chown -R "$EUID:runner" tree
printf 'ok\n'

cases.purpose: -R -L follows every symlink, so an internal dangling link cannot be dereferenced; the rest of the tree is still processed and the status is 1.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/sub
printf 'a\n' > tree/sub/a
ln -s missing-target tree/dangling
rc=0
chown -R -L "$EUID:runner" tree || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: -R with a valid directory and a missing operand changes the directory, diagnoses the missing one and exits 1.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/sub
rc=0
chown -R ":runner" tree missing || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: -f suppresses the diagnostic for a missing operand while keeping status 1.
cases.script:
rc=0
chown -Rf ":runner" missing || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: chown -v and -c describe each file as GNU does (retained, failed), for OWNER, OWNER:GROUP, :GROUP and OWNER: (G78).
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
: > a; mkdir -p d/e
n chown -v runner a
n chown -c runner a
n chown -v runner:runner a
n chown -v :runner a
n chown -v runner: a
n chown -v "$EUID" a
n chown -v '' a
n chown -Rv runner d
n chown -v runner nosuch | s
n chown -cf runner nosuch
n chown -v 0 a | s

cases.purpose: chown --recursive, --reference, --from, --dereference/--no-dereference, abbreviations and GNU diagnostics (G74).
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
: > a; : > b; ln -s a l; ln -s nosuch dl; mkdir -p d/e
n chown --recursive --verbose runner d
n chown --reference=b --verb a
n chown --from=runner --verbose runner a
n chown --from=0 -v runner a
n chown --no-dereference -v runner dl
n chown --dereference runner dl | s
n chown -R --dereference runner d | s
n chown --ref=nosuch a | s
n chown --bogus a | s
n chown runner | s

cases.purpose: OWNER[:GROUP] operand forms from the coreutils manual: names, numbers, a leading '+', 'OWNER:' login group, ':GROUP', ':', the empty operand, the legacy '.' separator and its warning, blanks before a number, and GNU's invalid user/group/spec diagnostics naming the whole operand.
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
g=$(/usr/bin/id -g)
: > a
for spec in runner runner: :runner "+$EUID" "$EUID:" "+$EUID:" "$EUID:runner" "runner:$g" "$EUID:+$g" runner.runner runner. .runner . .. : '' " $EUID" "$EUID " "+ $EUID" "0$EUID" + -0 +-1 +runner 4294967295 nosuch nosuch: nosuch:runner runner:nosuch :nosuch :+runner runner:runner:x abc.def "$EUID.$g" "$EUID."; do
  n chown -v -- "$spec" a | s
done

cases.purpose: Which -c/-v report GNU prints for a refused or impossible change: 'ownership' versus 'group', the old owner shown in the terms of the request, numeric versus named new owners, failures on a missing file (no 'from' part), and -c/-f silencing.
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
g=$(/usr/bin/id -g)
: > a
for spec in 0 :0 0:0 0:runner runner:0 :+0 "$EUID:0"; do n chown -v -- "$spec" a | s; done
n chown -c 0 a | s
n chown -vf 0 a
n chown -cf 0 a
for spec in :runner '' "$EUID:$g" :0 runner runner: 0; do n chown -v -- "$spec" nosuch | s; done
n chown -vf runner nosuch
n chown -cv runner a
n chown -vc runner a

cases.purpose: -R with -P (default), -H and -L, with and without -h/--dereference: which links are traversed, which are changed themselves, the post-order report sequence, and a link back to an ancestor directory that is changed but not entered.
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
g=$(/usr/bin/id -g)
mkdir -p t/u d/e; : > d/x; : > t/f; : > t/u/z; ln -s ../t d/lt; ln -s ../t/f d/lf; ln -s d ld; ln -s .. d/e/up
for o in -R -RP -RH -RL -RLh -RHh "-RH --dereference" "-RL --dereference" "-RP --dereference -H"; do
  echo "== $o"; n chown -v $o runner ld | s; n chown -c $o :runner ld | s
done
n chown -Rv runner ld/ | s

cases.purpose: Dangling links under each traversal mode (diagnostics and status; -c keeps GNU's unspecified 'from' text out of the comparison), a directory that cannot be read (reported, not changed), trailing slashes in operands, and -f.
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
g=$(/usr/bin/id -g)
mkdir -p d u/locked u/ok; : > u/ok/y; ln -s nosuch d/dl; ln -s nosuch dl
for o in -R -RH -RL -RLh -RHh ""; do echo "== $o"; n chown -c $o runner d dl | s; done
n chown -hv runner dl
n chown -Rv runner dl
chmod 000 u/locked
n chown -Rv :runner u | s
n chown -Rfv runner u
n chown -Rf runner u
chmod 700 u/locked
n chown -Rv runner u/ u// ./u/ok/ | s
n chown -v runner u/// | s
n chown -v runner '' | s

cases.purpose: --preserve-root refuses a recursive walk of '/' reached through a followed link or a trailing slash, with GNU's two-line diagnostic, while -P changes the link itself and the option is inert without -R; --no-preserve-root cancels it.
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
g=$(/usr/bin/id -g)
ln -s / lroot
n chown -RH --preserve-root runner lroot | s
n chown -RL --preserve-root runner lroot | s
n chown -R --preserve-root runner lroot/ | s
n chown -R --preserve-root runner lroot/. | s
n chown -Rfv --preserve-root runner lroot/ | s
n chown -Rv --preserve-root runner lroot
n chown -hv --preserve-root runner lroot
n chown -Rv --preserve-root --no-preserve-root runner lroot
mkdir -p e; ln -s ../lroot e/r
n chown -RLv --preserve-root runner e | s

cases.purpose: --from with each OWNER[:GROUP] form (matching, not matching, login group, legacy '.', invalid values parsed before other checks) and --reference (dereferenced, missing reference, report text naming the reference's owner and group).
cases.script:

s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }

: > a; : > b; ln -s b lb
for f in 0 :0 runner :runner runner: runner:runner "$EUID:$g" "+$EUID" '' :; do n chown -v --from="$f" runner a | s; n chown -v --from="$f" :runner a | s; done

n chown --reference=b | s
